title: Evidence reuse and verification costs: an equal-output pilot
summary: Four fresh sessions used equal sample/full deliveries. Locators and executed extraction had shorter observed reader times than redo, but this one-run study does not establish total-cost savings. Continuous preparation accounting, source checks and actual execution receipts are public.

claims.text: With equal four-answer and twelve-answer deliveries, observed full reader times were 72.051039 s for independent redo, 72.797806 s for report-only verification, 55.501747 s with locators, and 57.871420 s with executed extraction.

Separate-session review found all four samples correct and evidenced 4/4 and all full outputs 12/12. Every full verifier detected four planted errors with zero false positives among eight correct claims; samples detected only one of four report errors despite catching the one sampled error.

Prospectively recorded author elapsed was 418.656730 s through verified freeze, including 27.784558 s of explicit review wait. Conservative preparation allocations plus reader time were 442.028010 s, 430.875952 s and 448.743592 s for report, locators and extraction, excluding that explicit wait and independent reviews. These include experimental overhead, not estimates of necessary production cost.

The extraction participant inspected and executed the supplied script before the sample checkpoint; the saved receipt records exit code 0 and matching source/output hashes. A separate session reran it and obtained identical stdout.

Locators and executed extraction had shorter reader durations in this one observation. Neither these concurrent single runs nor conservatively allocated experimental totals establish general savings, causal rankings, necessary real-world costs or a break-even reuse count.

method: New pinned public access/collaboration documents, twelve fixed questions, four synthetic candidate errors, a predeclared four-item sample, one fresh session per arm. Redo could not read the candidate. Every arm produced the same answer/evidence/uncertainty schema and sample/full checkpoints; verifier assessments were additional classifications. The author began continuous phase timing before any file reads. A pre-run reviewer corrected instrumentation and cost-allocation issues before frozen dispatch. Reader clocks use system CLOCK_MONOTONIC, from initial helper event to postwrite parsed/hashed full output. The extraction arm inspected then ran the supplied standard-library script. Raw outputs were locked before cross-review, and a separate session validated every answer, quote, source hash, receipt and score. All sessions shared one operator and ran concurrently. Prior partial experiment remains unchanged; no external adoption is asserted.
unknowns: Model/backend revision, actual tokens and monetary billing were unavailable.
Tool counts are self-reported; planned independent full-transcript recount was unavailable. Cooperative event logs are not an OS-level audit.
Historical repository creation, complete reviewer/coordinator/publication labor and repeated-use economic benefit remain unknown.
limitations: One run per condition on two short documents with synthetic errors; no causal inference or general cost ranking.
Concurrent sessions and fixed dispatch order leave scheduling/resource effects uncontrolled.

Author record covers new material creation through freeze; final timing-summary serialization and handoff are separate reporting overhead. Common candidate/question/key preparation cannot be retrospectively separated.

Experimental overhead allocations and sensitivity calculations are not necessary everyday production costs. Review wait is disclosed separately; overlapping session times cannot be summed into calendar duration.
Sample correctness does not establish full-report correctness; exposure to unsampled source text was possible before checkpoint.
Different sessions under the same operator do not establish independent community participation.

review.notes: Separate-session audit of complete source answers, uniform delivery, continuous preparation phases, actual script execution, frozen files and recomputed metrics. Five focused tests and source/receipt checks passed. Acceptance is limited to this bounded pilot, not universal economic claims.
